owner.locales.title: Locale sync
owner.locales.body: Every language the live site can render, how much of each page it covers, and whether those figures come from the beta instance's working copy or from this deployment. Beta is re-read every few seconds, so a translation appears here as it is written.
owner.locales.notConfigured: The beta instance is not connected.
owner.locales.notConfiguredBody: This deployment is serving the catalogues it was built with. Set the beta origin to read new strings and languages as they are written — no restarts, no deploy.
owner.locales.liveBody: Read from {origin} {age}s ago. New and changed strings reach the browser on the next page load.
owner.locales.fallbackBody: Beta could not be read ({error}), so the site is serving this deployment's own files until it answers.
owner.locales.buildBody: These are the catalogues built into this deployment.
owner.locales.synced: The beta catalogues were read again.
owner.locales.autoBody: While this is on, this deployment checks beta for new catalogues every few seconds and picks up translations without a deploy. Turn it off to keep the current copy and sync only when you press Sync now.
owner.locales.autoHint: Manual mode stops the background poll; Sync now still reads beta immediately.
owner.locales.autoDisabled: Automatic locale syncing disabled — use Sync now.
owner.locales.panelBody: The status panel in the support servers can also show a translation coverage card: each language's share of the site and the bot, live from beta. Turn it on here and the card appears the next time the panel refreshes.
owner.locales.panelToggle: Show the translation card on the status panel
owner.locales.panelHint: Changes land on the panel's next refresh, within a minute. The panel is posted by the bot, so nothing is re-sent to Discord.
owner.locales.panelEnabled: Translation card shown on the status panel
owner.locales.panelDisabled: Translation card hidden on the status panel
owner.locales.languagesBody: Coverage counts every English key on the site's pages and in the bot's cog catalogues, so a language's percentage describes the whole product rather than half of it. A catalogue counts as done only when its file covers every English key.
owner.locales.cataloguesBody: Each catalogue folds open into its coverage per language — a website page or a bot cog. The bar is how much of that catalogue the language covers: a dash means no file yet, amber means a translation that started, green means complete.
owner.locales.botSectionBody: Every cog's message catalogue, counted against its own English keys. This is the wording the running bot sends in Discord.
owner.locales.siteSectionBody: The site's own page catalogues, counted against their English keys.
owner.updates.title: Zero-downtime updates
owner.updates.body: Pull the selected parts of this deployment straight from the beta instance. Each area applies the way it has to: files for the website, a reload for cogs, a module purge for utilities, a Flask rebuild for the API, re-imported event handlers, a ready-handler rebind for the startup writers, and an in-place restart for the bot core. Nothing restarts unless its own area changed.
owner.updates.areasBody: Switch on the areas to pull from beta. Areas without changes are up to date and stay off.
owner.updates.notConfigured: The update feed is not configured.
owner.updates.notConfiguredBody: Set the beta origin and the shared update token to stage files from beta. Without both, this page can only report what is already deployed.
owner.updates.noTokenBody: BETA_UPDATE_TOKEN must match on beta and here before beta will serve its files.
owner.updates.refreshed: Feed refreshed · {count} files waiting from beta.
owner.updates.botWarning: The bot core update replaces this process's own image on this deployment's listening socket. The port stays bound and the PID does not change, so a hosted service never restarts the container and the pulled files stay. Expect a few seconds where commands are not answered; the site keeps serving throughout.
owner.updates.lastBody: Run {id}. Every replaced file is kept under data/updates/backups.
owner.area.website: Replaces the built site. Flask serves the folder from disk, so the next request is the new site with nothing restarted.
owner.area.cogs: Drops the cached cog modules and reloads only the changed extensions, so the new file is what imports.
owner.area.utils: Purges the changed utility modules, reloads the extensions that import them, and rebuilds the dashboard.
owner.area.webapp: Re-imports the API and swaps the new Flask app into the running server. The listening socket never closes.
owner.area.database: Re-imports src/events/startup/database.py and runs its setup again: missing tables, columns and migrations are applied to the live database. The process keeps running.
owner.area.events: Re-imports the gateway event modules and rebinds the handlers bot.py calls, so the next message runs the new code with nothing restarted.
owner.area.startup: Re-imports the startup data writers and rebinds the ready handler, then refreshes the stats and command files. No restart and no cog reload.
owner.area.bot: Restarts this process in place on the listening socket it already owns, so the port never closes and nothing recreates the service.
